lastCommit.message:
The slate takes the weight

CONTRACTS INTERACTION PASS. The second iteration of the second UI pass, bounded
to the four families the owner named on the device, and nothing else.

FOUR FAMILIES WERE NAMED. FOUR WERE DEFICIENT — BUT ONLY THREE LOOKED IT.

⚠ 1. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE — a `TouchableOpacity` at `activeOpacity={0.85}`, so a
15% fade on the largest press surface on the screen was not a choice but a
ceiling: a TouchableOpacity has no `({ pressed }) => …` style callback and no
render-prop children, so the depth language is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE inside
one. Same finding as OTA-1805's room doors and OTA-1810's dossier, at a third
door. It now reports the press, takes `kit.controlPressed` for the travel and
the ring, and stops standing on its chassis planes while it is held.

⚠⚠ IT MINTS NO NEW MATERIAL, AND OTA-1810's DOSSIER REASONING DELIBERATELY DOES
NOT TRANSFER. That rim was already an asymmetric lit/dark pair, so borrowing
generic colours would have replaced its material and a pressed record would have
stopped looking like a filed record. This ring is one uniform gold; minting a
second gold to invert it would invent material AND push against the gold
ratchet, which is shrink-only with no headroom. The card's identity — its 1.5dp
gold sides, its gold tag, its gold phase line — is untouched, and the shared
press owns two edges for exactly as long as a finger is down.

⚠ 2. CONTRACTS / COLLECTIBLES TABS — `TouchableOpacity` at 0.7, and this family
needed a DIFFERENT answer rather than the same one. `tabBtn` is an UNDERLINE
tab: no fill, no ring, and the ONE mark that says SELECTED is
`borderBottomColor` going gold. `kit.controlPressed` writes that exact field.

⚠⚠ SO THE MECHANICAL REPAIR WOULD HAVE DRAWN A LIT UNDERLINE ON AN UNSELECTED
TAB — PRESSED would have looked like SELECTED, which is the one thing a tab
contract cannot allow. Two structural answers, both ordering rather than
cleverness: `tabBtnPressed` hands the bottom edge back as `transparent` so a
press cannot forge the selection mark, and `tabBtnActive` is LAST in every
array so a genuinely selected tab keeps its gold all the way through. The
player gets the face lighting and the tab travelling — family-appropriate for
a thing with no sidewall to collapse.

⚠ AboutScreen's same-named `tabBtn` DOES take `controlPressed` whole, and that
is not an inconsistency: its selected state is a BACKGROUND swap on a fully
ringed chip, so there is no semantic border for the press to overwrite.

⚠ 3. MILESTONE CELLS — `TouchableOpacity` at 0.7, and the fade landed on a bare
`flex: 1` layout wrapper. The CELL — the object with the border, the radius and
the chassis planes, the thing the player can actually see — was never told a
finger was on it. `pressed` is now a second parameter of the same renderer; the
read-only contract still passes `false` and is byte-identical.

⚠⚠⚠ 4. THE SORT / FILTER BARS, AND THIS IS THE ONE WORTH READING. They were
already `Pressable`. They already consumed a live `pressed` in the style array.
Every census this repository owns — OTA-1804's construction ledger, OTA-1806's
plane ratchet — reads that as REPAIRED. What `sortBarPressed` actually drew was
`{ opacity: 0.7 }`: the whole-control fade the owner's ruling calls insufficient
and that OTA-1806 removed from COMPLETE / ABANDON / DISCARD in this very file.
Three sites survived that sweep BECAUSE they consumed `pressed`. Presence is not
participation, and this is the second distinct shape of that error shipped here.
`sortBarPressed` is deleted, not renamed; nothing referenced it.

Their planes moved from `TAB_PLANES` to `ctlPlanes(pressed)`, and that moves
NOTHING at rest: the suite asserts by value that `tabPlane*` and `controlPlane*`
are the same three heights, offsets and colours, because the kit built an
inactive tab at "the command's own weight". A safe swap by measurement, not by
reading a comment.

PROVEN EXCLUSION. The slate filter (ALL / ACTIVE / PARKED) already reported its
press, already travelled, and already kept its selection through it. Untouched —
and §6 of the suite makes that claim falsifiable rather than decorative, the
same discipline OTA-1810 applied to REPLAY OPENING.

⚠⚠⚠ A CROSS-GAME PRIMITIVE WAS NOT SPENT UNDER A CONTRACTS AUTHORIZATION.
`TTabBar` — the kit's shared tab component — carries the identical defect
(TouchableOpacity, activeOpacity 0.7, no pressed state) and is rendered by
GuidanceScreen, VendorScreen and CraftingScreen. Converting it here would have
restyled three unrelated screens under a Contracts job. It is reported and left
alone. This screen was reachable without it because it owns its tabs locally,
which is the fact that made the repair boundable at all.

⚠⚠⚠ ONE EXISTING SUITE WAS CHANGED, AND IT IS DISCLOSED HERE RATHER THAN BURIED.
`ota1361ClimbsToggleAndGlow` presses SORT BY DISTANCE the way a player does —
it finds the control by its label and calls its handler, which is the right way
to write it. But its `elementTexts` walker read `props.children` as a static
element tree, and a Pressable that feeds `pressed` to its planes renders its
children as a FUNCTION. The moment the sort bar was repaired the label went
invisible to the walker, the finder returned zero nodes, and a suite about
SORTING failed on its ability to locate a BUTTON.

NOT ONE SORTING ASSERTION WAS TOUCHED. Only the locator moved, and it moved to
cover MORE controls than before — every depressing control in the game renders
this way now. It is load-bearing after the change as well as before: NC-7
replaces the climb section's shared comparator with the unsorted list and the
named test goes red.

AT REST NOTHING MOVED. Every style this OTA introduces is behind `pressed`, and
§3 of the suite walks each one and asserts it.

EVIDENCE on the exact committed tree:
  focused suite ota1811TheSlateTakesTheWeight  43/43
  37 suites that read ContractsScreen  612/612
  22/22 check:* gates · lint clean · source typecheck clean
  typecheck:tests at baseline 201 — NOT raised
  AUTHORITATIVE TRACKED FAST SURFACE (scratchpad/ excluded, CI-equivalent):
        1,306 suites passed / 1,306 total
        14,195 passed · 3 skipped · 0 failed · 518.1 s · jest exit 0
        (1,305 at OTA-1810 plus this OTA's one new suite — it reconciles exactly)

  ⚠ AND LOCAL DISCOVERY DID INCLUDE SCRATCHPAD, REPORTED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN
  QUIETLY. The repo's own `test:ci:fast` passes `--testPathIgnorePatterns
  /node_modules/`, which REPLACES jest's defaults, and there is no scratchpad
  ignore in the config — so the first local run discovered 1,354 suites / 14,303
  tests (also all green) because 48 untracked `scratchpad/**/*.test.*` probes
  were swept in. CI checks out from git and never sees them; 1,354 − 48 = 1,306.
  The 1,306 figure is the authoritative one. scratchpad/ is NOT deleted.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each reverted with md5 match and zero residue:
  NC-CONTRACTS-1  PRIMARY OBJECTIVE press defeated        → 1 red (named)
  NC-CONTRACTS-2  tab pressed face defeated               → 2 red
  NC-CONTRACTS-3  sort/filter planes refrozen             → 1 red (named)
  NC-CONTRACTS-4  milestone cell pressed style defeated   → 2 red
  NC-CONTRACTS-4b the finger never reaches the renderer   → 1 red (named)
  NC-CONTRACTS-5  a tab's selection reordered before its press → 2 red
  NC-CONTRACTS-6  the card's planes frozen through the press   → 1 red (named)
  NC-CONTRACTS-7  the climb section stops obeying the sort → 1 red in ota1361
No negative control mutated protected artwork or gameplay.

⚠ TWO OF THIS SUITE'S OWN WEAKNESSES WERE FOUND BY ITS NEGATIVE CONTROLS AND
FIXED BEFORE COMMIT, not written around: NC-4 first CRASHED the file at module
load because the milestone locator keyed on the very text the repair introduces
(a suite that cannot load proves only that it cannot load), and the milestone
ordering assertion compared two indices without asserting both were present, so
deleting the press left `-1` on the left of a `>` and the claim passed while the
repair was gone.

ADJACENT, PROVEN DEFICIENT, DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED — outside the four named
families, reported so the gap is visible rather than silent:
  · ContractsScreen:956  the Capital "tap to travel" rows inside the PRIMARY
    OBJECTIVE tracker — TouchableOpacity, activeOpacity 0.7
  · ContractsScreen:2497 the COLLECTIBLES story accordion header — same shape
  · ContractsScreen:2924 `contractsNoticePressed: { opacity: 0.7 }` — the same
    presence-not-participation defect as `sortBarPressed`, on the notice strip
  · tartariaKit TTabBar — the cross-game tab primitive, 3 consumer screens

Classification: A the screen · B the new suite · C the OTA stamp and the widened
locator · P/F: ZERO.

GOLEM AND HAL. This commit carries no [ota-hal] marker; it publishes to Golem
automatically, and the same validated SHA is then promoted to HAL through the
exact-SHA promotion control plane. HAL is the main line.

PHYSICAL VERIFICATION IS STILL REQUIRED and is NOT claimed. Whether any of this
is perceptible under a thumb is the owner's eye.
